title: Quenched SLE₃ limits for general weak random-bond Ising models
main_claim: Take bonds J_e = 1 + εξ_e, where the ξ_e are iid with any bounded, mean-zero, nondegenerate law ρ. For ε below some ε_0(ρ), at the magnetization threshold β_c^ρ(ε), the quenched Dobrushin interface converges in environmental probability to chordal SLE_3 in the oriented uniform-curve bounded-Lipschitz metric, for any Jordan domain and any deterministic lattice approximation. The paper also proves β_c^ρ(ε) = K0 + O_ρ(ε²).

issues.location: sections/scale.tex Prop. scale-estimates; sections/crossings.tex (whole section); sections/interface.tex Prop. strip-transfer and the strip/barrier input
issues.description: Most of the analytic machinery is imported from companion papers R and S. That includes the one-step and marginal-variance-flow estimates, the local scale map and its reversal marks, the crossing bootstrap, the pure buffered RSW inputs, and the finite-strip-to-limiting-barrier lemma. I spot-checked R's variance-flow proof (Shell calculation, variance.tex). It already keeps the cubic terms, handles the mean pieces separately, and uses only that independent groups are centred. So the claim that the import needs no symmetry of the disorder law holds up there. I did not re-verify the other imports line by line. This is a dependency note, not a demonstrated gap.
issues.evidence: "Thus an asymmetric law does not require any alteration of the imported estimates."

coverage:
I read every section of the LaTeX: introduction, scale, tuning, matching, crossings, criticality and interface, plus the references. Checks done:
- Dual coupling derivatives with sympy: g(K0)=K0, g'(K0)=-1, g''(K0)=2√2.
- Lemma initial-coordinates: the primal and dual expansions, d_ρ, m_0 = 2s_0·E(K̃-K0), W_0 = 2Var, and C_ρ = 2K0²σ².
- Shooting argument: the order of constants (A, D, T, B, H), the inward norm bounds, the outward mean walls ((L-1)D > C_1A²), the variance trap and the nested-interval continuity.
- Cross-check of the β_c shift: matching β_p = β_d forces a shift of K0²σ²ε²/√2. This agrees independently with the condition E log(e^{2βJ}-1) = log √2.
- Torus duality: prefactor a(K) = ∏√sinh 2K_e, the entries of H against the intersection-pairing signs, H² = I, and the ratio formula.
- Matching via OSSS with every edge queried, plus FK monotonicity.
- Annular FK barriers and the product bound over disjoint bond neighbourhoods.
- Amplified dual-arm decay: union bound, revealment C·N^{-d}, logit integration.
- Primal percolation above β_* from the dual-circuit sum, and the identity magnetization = percolation.
- Conditional gluing constant 6/c (my derivation gives 2e/c + 4e/c).
- Ordered-chords lemma, the progress/six-passage lemma, and the final BL/Markov step.
- I also read R's variance-flow proof to confirm it does not use symmetry of the disorder.
